facts.fact: ICTD says mobile money is the most common way to pay taxes online in Benin, with a fee of 1% capped at FCFA 1,000.
ICTD says taxpayers in Benin can create their own account, file and pay online through SIGIBé, which reached small businesses in 2024.
ICTD, citing the DGI's 2025 activity report, says electronic payments in Benin exceed 96% for most taxes, driven largely by medium and large firms.

ICTD says SIGIBé, which replaced SIGTAS (launched 2018), was rolled out for large and medium taxpayers in 2022 and extended to small businesses in 2024, with the Cotonou centres online since May 2024 and taxpayers able to file online.
ICTD says taxpayers in Benin pay online through SIGIBé, mostly by mobile money, and the DGI reports electronic payments above 96% for most taxes.
ICTD says taxpayers in Benin register for the tax identification number (IFU) on the SIGIBé platform.
ICTD says registering for the IFU now requires the national personal identification number, which the system verifies directly with ANIP.
